NATO put a price tag on the map in Ankara. Iran buried Khamenei as missiles tested the Hormuz ceasefire. China fired a missile into the South Pacific. Macron walked Damascus. A Paris court held France's 2027 map.

5 ways the lines shifted this week — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ NATO's 32 leaders met in Ankara with one theme: money. Record European defence budgets, ~$40bn for anti-drone tech — and fears the US arms industry, drained by Ukraine and Iran, can't supply allies. Zelensky pressed for air defence after Kyiv strikes. (BBC, Guardian, AJ, NYT)

2/ Millions mourned Ali Khamenei in Tehran before his burial in Mashhad — as the US-Iran ceasefire was tested at the Strait of Hormuz: a tanker ablaze off Oman, and a US official saying Iranian missiles hit two ships. (BBC, Guardian, AJ, DW, NYT)

3/ Hours after Australia signed a defence pact with Fiji, China test-fired a long-range ballistic missile into the South Pacific. Canberra: "destabilising." Solomon Is.: "be our friend but don't threaten us." The Pacific is now contested space. (Guardian, NYT)

4/ Macron became the first EU leader to visit Syria since Assad's fall, meeting President al-Sharaa — as two blasts hit a busy Damascus street near his hotel. He was unhurt. France drew Syria's borders a century ago; now it's back. (BBC, AJ, DW, NYT)

5/ A Paris appeals court ruled this week on Marine Le Pen's embezzlement conviction — and the office ban that could bar the 2027 frontrunner from the race. Either outcome redraws France's electoral map. (BBC, Guardian, AJ, NYT)

The map behind story 1: military spending as a share of GDP, 2025. Ukraine is literally off the scale — no country close. Russia deep red, NATO's eastern flank darkening, most of the world pale. Data: Our World in Data (CC BY)
